passages.text: The lecture assigns Sculley et al., Hidden technical debt in machine learning systems, defines technical debt as not-quite-right code postponed, asks students to identify concrete hidden debts, and depicts a nine-stage ML workflow with feedback loops from evaluation and monitoring to earlier stages.

The fairness lifecycle asks teams to scrutinize system vision for allocation, quality-of-service, stereotyping, denigration, and representation harms, and to revise systems when benchmarks reveal harm or document why mitigation is not possible.
The privacy lecture identifies model stealing, model inversion, and unintended memorization as confidentiality and privacy attacks.
